renders: landing site /docs/installation/ — human render (getff-ai-site S1; the first-steps-* quick-start slugs are stubs per face spec §4, so the render target is the Installation page — BU-F14 re-point, S0a)

core.goal: install -> a rule provably fires on your code
core.profileFlag: --profile core (core is never the default — install.sh:648 makes the non-interactive default `env`)

steps.title: Install at core depth
steps.action: From your project root run `bash <getff>/setup -y --profile core <stack>` — `core` must be named, because `-y` on its own resolves to `env` (install.sh:648). (stacks: ts-server, react-next, react-spa, react-native; `python`, `cargo` and `go` are separate non-npm toolchain lanes, each an explicit positional — `./setup cargo` or `bash install.sh cargo`, the wrapper forwards lanes verbatim). Omit the stack to auto-detect.

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/` — you should see AGENTS.md, `.ai-factory/{DESCRIPTION.md,ARCHITECTURE.md,RULES.md}` and `scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh`. Nothing here is optional; a missing file means the install did not finish.

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md` (domain, stack, constraints, non-goals). This is the file AGENTS.md sends every future session to first, so a passport left unfilled degrades every later session.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh` — fails when a shipped custom rule matches ZERO files in your layout, i.e. it is installed but silently enforcing nothing. If it fires, widen `RULE_GLOBS` in `eslint.config.mjs` to cover your layout. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.
steps.evidence: scripts/check-rule-globs.sh (shipped at core; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Watch a rule actually fire
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` — plants deliberately-bad input in a temp dir and asserts the installed ESLint rules go RED on it. This is the first-rule-fires moment: an installed rule that has never been seen to fire is an unproven claim.

steps.title: Fire a rule on YOUR code, not a fixture
steps.action: Plant one violation of a shipped getff rule in YOUR tree and run your stack's native gate — the RED line names your file. npm: add `z.string().parse(input)` to a file under a boundary glob (`**/routes/**`, `**/handlers/**`, `**/controllers/**`, `**/app/api/**`, `**/actions/**`), run `npm run lint` — RED from `rules-as-tests/no-unsafe-zod-parse` (R2, the one custom rule wired unconditionally; R7/R8 fire only under `AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1`). Lanes: python — add `datetime.utcnow()`, run `ruff check . --config .getff/ruff-bans.toml`; cargo — add `std::env::var("X")`, run `cargo clippy`; go — add `os.Getenv("X")`, run `golangci-lint run`.
steps.evidence: templates/ts-server/eslint.config.mjs:179 (R2 unconditional); setup.d/70-deps.sh:75 (npm run lint); setup.d/45-python.sh:587 / 46-cargo.sh:256 / 47-go.sh:252 (lane firing self-checks)

steps.title: Run the gate you will run every day
steps.action: `bash scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh` — drift + code-vs-docs probes (~10 sec). Expect findings on a fresh project; the INSTALL-FOR-AI «Expected first-run failures» table lists which ones are normal.

steps.title: Continue into rule research in the same session
steps.action: Invoke `/rule-research` (or read `.claude/agents/rule-researcher.md` on a harness without skills). The installer delivered a curated starter set; researching stack-specific rules from live documentation is the next step of the same lifecycle, not a later project.

env.goal: core + the multi-model contour surface: tier criteria on disk and one idea through /arch

steps.title: Install at env depth
steps.action: `bash <getff>/install.sh <stack> --profile env`. Already on core? Re-run that same command — the deeper payload is added and every core artefact stays byte-identical except `.prettierignore`, whose managed block gains the new paths. Do not reach for `--refresh` to upgrade: it re-delivers fixes to what you already have and does not reliably deepen an install — on a `core` project `--refresh --profile env` exits 0 while `tier-home.md` and `.claude/skills/arch/` stay absent.
steps.evidence: install.sh:1342-1350 — the tier-home refresh arm is presence-gated («refresh must not create it on core»); `arch` is in no do_refresh skill loop. Measured on a core consumer against staging 2026-08-09: `--refresh --profile env` → exit 0, tier-home NO, arch NO (the worktree-scripts arm at install.sh:1251-1256 was ungated and delivered 4 env-tier scripts on a core project; it has carried the env|factory|presence gate since #1334, so that depth-boundary defect is closed); plain `--profile env` → exit 0, tier-home YES, arch YES, every pre-existing core file byte-identical except .prettierignore. Also INSTALL-FOR-AI.md «Install depth profiles»

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/` plus `.ai-factory/tier-home.md` and the five skills env adds over core: `.claude/skills/arch/`, `.claude/skills/night-mode/`, `.claude/skills/orchestrator/`, `.claude/skills/pipeline/` and `.claude/skills/reviewer/`.
steps.evidence: setup.d/30-templates.sh (tier-home at env+); verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md`.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh`, then `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` to see a rule go RED on planted input. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md`. It owns the Tier 0/1/2 routing criteria and the capability-absence degradation matrix — what still works when there is no aif runtime, no executor-tier model, or a non-Claude-Code harness. AGENTS.md only points here; the criteria live in this one file.

steps.title: Take one idea through `/arch`
steps.action: Invoke `/arch <topic>` — the external design contour turns a raw idea into a reviewed design plus a routed handoff. On a harness without skills, read `.claude/skills/arch/SKILL.md` and follow it by hand.
steps.evidence: .claude/skills/arch/SKILL.md (shipped at env+; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

factory.goal: env + one task driven through the pipeline

steps.title: Install at factory depth
steps.action: `bash <getff>/install.sh <stack> --profile factory`. Pick this ONLY if this machine runs the aif-handoff operator runtime — the factory payload dead-ends without it.

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls .claude/skills/` — on top of env you should see `.claude/skills/dispatcher/`, `.claude/skills/aif-doctor/`, `.claude/skills/harvest/`, `.claude/skills/story/` and `.claude/skills/claude-glm-executor-handoff/`. `pipeline` and `night-mode` are NOT factory additions — they arrive with env+ and are already there.
steps.evidence: setup.d/10-skills.sh; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md`.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh`, then `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` to see a rule go RED on planted input. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md` — it decides which tier a task routes to, and what degrades when a capability is absent.

steps.title: Write your first kickoff
steps.action: Create `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/<work-item>/kickoff.md`: a `Type:` line (`fix` / `research` / `feature`), the goal, and — if the work splits into parallel sub-steps — a `## §1 Sub-wave` section with one table row per sub-step.

steps.title: Ask the pipeline what to start next
steps.action: Invoke `/pipeline`. It reads your kickoffs plus `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/plan.md` (created on first run), ranks them, and emits a launch table. An empty backlog reports «nothing queued» — that is normal, not an error.
steps.evidence: .claude/skills/pipeline/SKILL.md (shipped at env+; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Dispatch the top row and read the result
steps.action: Dispatch the launch table's top row, then bring the finished branch back with `/harvest`. If a task stalls or the runtime misbehaves, `/aif-doctor` is the diagnostic entry point.
